notes: §1989:A.2.29.3 AR1: "Argument-1 must be a nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric data item whose content has one of the following two formats", with "digit is a string of one to 18 digits". CheckArgumentClasses screens the Verified NUMVAL row at every edition: Violation refuses a numeric or alphabetic argument and PredicateViolation's category arm refuses an edited item, which is the 1985 sense of an alphanumeric item (§1985:VI.5.9.4); national arguments are refused at 85 by the edition gate (COBOL0900). NumvalDec returns the exact value NvScan parses, and NvScan accepts both 1989 formats (probed at 85: leading sign, trailing + - CR DB, "12.", ".5", 18 digits with nine decimals); its 2023 widenings (lowercase cr/db, up to 31 digits) only give a value where 1989 leaves the result undefined. The witness runs a trailing CR and a leading sign with embedded spaces. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs#VisitNonNumericLiteral (kb/Work PB5416: the version pass's statement-scoped national/boolean literal gate is deleted; the literal token's format gate, LiteralScreen.GateFormat, refuses N, NX, B and BX literals at 85 wherever they are written)

next.reason: 1985: "Argument-1 must be a nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric data item ... digit is a string of one to 18 digits"; 2023: "alphanumeric or national literal or ... data item ... total number of digits in argument-1 shall not exceed 31". 2023 adds national arguments and lowercase CR/DB, and replaces the 18-digit limit per digit string with a total limit of 31, 34 or 35 digits depending on the arithmetic in effect.
